AP accrual cutoff

Finds goods received and work done with no bill yet at month end, drafts the accrual and its reversal, and keeps open orders out.

Watch someone use it

Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, AP accruals at 30 September 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

Claudewith the MosoFin ap accrual cutoff skill

What AP do we need to accrue for September?

Claude

I can work that out. Before I read anything, I need seven answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.

  1. Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
  2. Which period, with exact dates? And do you keep the books on the accrual basis or the cash basis?
  3. Where do you log goods receipts? Do you have service confirmations or time sheets?
  4. How many days after month end do I search for late bills? I propose the day that the books close.
  5. Which account holds accrued liabilities?
  6. Can you recover input tax, and in which country?
  7. Optional: which materiality threshold applies to accruals? Is it tighter at year end? Without one, I accrue everything that I find.

Use MosoFin. 1 to 30 September, accrual basis. The warehouse logs every delivery in a sheet, attached. We close on 10 October. Use Accrued Expenses. We recover no input tax. Materiality is $500 all year.

I search for late bills from 1 to 10 October. Accruals go to Accrued Expenses, with no input-tax line. Materiality is $500.

No tool can see your inbox. Please send me each bill that came in after 30 September and is not in the books yet. Then shall I start?

Crestline billed $1,000 in each of June, July and August. Its contract letter says $1,500. Which amount do I use?

The list is right, but take out Power Co. Our other accruals run already has the electricity. Crestline's new contract is right.

Claude

First, the goods. Your books hold orders but no goods receipts, so the quantities come from your log. I searched every open order, back to PO-2033 from 14 July:

Goods received, not invoiced
PO-2041 line 1, 400 × $12.00, GRN-0917 on 29 Sep$4,800.00
+ PO-2033 line 2, 90 received × $20.00$1,800.00
+ PO-2033 line 1, received and billed on RW-8812$0.00
+ PO-2044, nothing received$0.00
= Goods received, not invoiced$6,600.00

RW-8812 has no order number. I matched it by supplier, date, amount and description, and I mark the match as inferred. The other $4,200 of open orders did not arrive. That is an order, not a debt, so I do not accrue it.

Claude

Stock rises by $6,600 and September cost rises by $8,050. Accrued Expenses opened at $1,950, and both August reversals posted. So it closes at $14,650. A person posts these entries. I do not. Do you want the workpaper as an Excel file?
